$description: Wave 5 (W5 Selection, D-023/D-024) component tokens for Rating. Aliases semantic/* only. Same accent-scarcity reasoning as checkbox.json/radio.json/switch.json — a Rating routinely renders several *selected* stars at once (a 4-star rating has 4 filled stars in one view), so the scarce brand accent (`color.action.primary`) stays off this control per braun-flat.md rule 3; `selected` reuses `color.role.neutral.solid` instead. `unselected` reuses `color.border.interactive` (D-014 pattern already used by Radio's ring/Checkbox's border/Switch's track-off) rather than the quieter `border.hairline` — the outline star is a graphical/UI-component boundary that must clear the 3:1 WCAG non-text minimum, not the 1.3:1 hairline was designed for. `disabled` reuses `color.text.disabled` for both filled and outline stars (WCAG contrast minimums are exempt for disabled controls, same exemption input.json documents — inactive, not read as content). Contrast self-check (computed from resolved hex in packages/tokens/build/css/{light,dark}.css, relative-luminance formula): selected-vs-canvas 8.20:1 (light) / 7.94:1 (dark), unselected-vs-canvas 3.72:1 (light) / 3.72:1 (dark) — both clear their respective minimums (4.5:1 n/a since selected exceeds it anyway; 3:1 UI-component minimum for unselected) in both themes. The selected/unselected distinction is NOT color-only: the star SVG itself swaps between an outline path (unselected) and a filled path (selected) — a real shape cue per BLUEPRINT §7 / braun-flat rule 4, verified structurally (which of the two child `<svg>` elements has `display:block`) rather than by color alone, so it survives `forced-colors` mode where this color pair collapses to the same system color.
